content: Lifestyle modifications, such as participating in stress reduction programs, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and making dietary changes (e.g., avoiding caffeine, fatty foods, and certain spices), can enhance the effectiveness of this medication. If you are taking this medication on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature. It can also be stored in the refrigerator to improve its taste, but do not freeze it. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication, commonly known by brand names such as Alternagel and Amphojel, is used to treat symptoms caused by excessive stomach acid, including stomach upset, heartburn, and acid indigestion. Aluminum hydroxide is an antacid that works quickly to neutralize existing stomach acid. However, it does not prevent the production of stomach acid. To use this medication, take it orally between meals and at bedtime. Follow all instructions on the product packaging or as directed by your doctor. Shake the bottle well before each dose. Refrigerating the suspension may improve its flavor, but do not freeze it. This medication is most effective when taken without other fluids. This product contains aluminum, which can interact with other medications (such as digoxin, iron, tetracycline antibiotics, pazopanib, and quinolone antibiotics like ciprofloxacin), potentially reducing their absorption in the body. If your acid-related symptoms persist or worsen after using this product for one week, or if you suspect a serious medical problem, seek medical attention immediately. If you are using this medication daily for more than two weeks, consult your doctor, as you may have an underlying condition requiring different treatment. Constipation is a possible side effect of this medication, which can lead to complications such as hemorrhoids or bowel obstruction. To reduce the risk of constipation, drink plenty of fluids and engage in regular physical activity. Using an antacid containing magnesium alongside this product may help prevent constipation. Stool softeners may also be beneficial. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Aluminum-containing antacids can bind to phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract, which may result in low phosphate levels, particularly if you have normal kidney function and use large doses for an extended period. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking aluminum hydroxide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It may pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Antacids can interfere with the absorption of many other drugs. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance.
